english.title: Contravene provision of EU Regulation relating to pain, distress and suffering at time of killing animal under Art 3
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[contravened]_
(B)_[caused or permitted **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to contravene]_

a provision of Council Regulation (EC) No 1099/2009 of 24 September 2009 on the protection of animals at the time of killing, namely

(C)_[Article 3(1) relating to the general requirement to spare an animal avoidable pain, distress or suffering]_
(D)_[Article 3(2) relating to measures to protect animals from avoidable pain, distress or suffering]_
(E)_[Article 3(3) relating to facilities for killing and related operations]_

in that **(..SPECIFY CONTRAVENTION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 30(1)(g) and 33(2) of the Welfare of Animals at the Time of Killing (England) Regulations 2015.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Contravention of a provision in Schedule 5 to the regulations is an offence except where it is not necessary to comply with the provision by virtue of (i) an exemption or transitional provision specified in the EU Regulation; or(ii) a derogation granted by the competent authority under Article 18(3) in relation to a depopulation operationFor contravention of an Article other than Article 3, please see H19058

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions
6 monthsNote
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
